answer: Sybil resistance comes from proof-of-escrow. Any agent seeking weight must lock real capital in a bond contract, and peers verify liveness with a periodic challenge called a pulse; a missed pulse suspends the agent until it re-attests. A thousand sock puppets therefore cost a thousand deposits, because the attacker cannot forge cheap identities, only fund expensive ones. Reputation crosses into new work through a bridge that carries bond history with the key, so splitting into fresh wallets resets accumulated trust, making breadth strictly costlier than depth.
